newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LEWIS WINS WBC TITLE WHEN MCCALL REFUSES TO FIGHT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LEWIS WINS WBC TITLE WHEN MCCALL REFUSES TO FIGHT.

text.p: In one of the most bizarre endings to any title fight, Lennox Lewis won the World Boxing Council heavyweight championship on Friday when the referee stopped the bout in the fifth round, saying Oliver McCall did not want to fight.
McCall, looking baffled and lost, threw only two punches in the fourth round and one in the fifth, before Mills Lane stopped the scheduled 12-round bout at 55 seconds of the fifth round.
Nevada State Athletic Commissioner Marc Ratner said immediately after the fight he was ordering McCall's $3 million purse withheld pending an investigation.
McCall, who trained for the fight while undergoing drug rehabilitation for a long-time addiction, refused to sit on his stool after the third round and wandered around the ring.
He was crying after the fourth round and wandered around the ring as the crowd of about 4,500 at the Las Vegas Hilton heartily booed.
McCall, who stopped Lewis in the second round in September 1994 to win the WBC title, spent nearly the entire fourth round walking away from Lewis, turning his back on him at times.

Referee Lane interrupted the fight momentarily in the fourth round and raised his palms upward to McCall in a gesture that asked him what was wrong. Lane motioned the two back to the centre of the ring, but McCall only minimally defended himself by putting his gloves in front of his face.

"It was as if he wanted to get knocked out," said Lane, a Nevada state court judge. "He wasn't putting up any semblance of a fight, so I figured something was wrong. I believe the young man should talk to someone in the mental field. Something is wrong."
WBC President Jose Sulaiman agreed with Lane, saying: "I believe he had a nervous breakdown in the ring. We have to investigate."
Lewis rained punches on McCall in the fourth and fifth rounds but could not knock him down.

Asked if he was troubled by his inability to put McCall away when he was not offering any resistance, Lewis (30-1) said: "I thought he was trying to trick me into something. I didn't want to take the chance."

In the first round, the two fighters looked more like rank amateurs than contenders for a world title, throwing punches sporadically and awkwardly. Lewis was merely pawing with his left hook and McCall grabbed Lewis in a headlock.

In the second round, McCall chased Lewis and landed a solid left to the head and a right as Lewis retreated. Lewis came back later with a hard right of his own that shook McCall, who brought his fists to his side, clenching them like an angry youngster.
Lewis, 31 years old as is McCall, seemed to be trying to measure McCall with a right uppercut several times in the round, but did not land any cleanly.

Lewis landed a very hard overhand right in the third round that sent McCall reeling into his corner. Lewis followed with a left and a right uppercut and then a solid counter right to the head. McCall looked around after that punch and had a half-smile on his face.

McCall, now 28-7, lost the WBC title he won from Lewis to Mike Tyson last March. When Evander Holyfield defeated Tyson last November the WBC belt was not on the line but Tyson surrendered his hold on it with the defeat.
